title: Integral ring-object constructibility and the completed category
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Z$ be a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible: $Z$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], so it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, a finite bound on chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring. Put $B_Z=p_Z^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Identify it with $\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/\varpi^n)_Z$ by the canonical coefficient-limit map [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. In the ordinary category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_Z))$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], for every $K$ the following conditions are equivalent:

(i) $K$ is bounded constructible in the general ring-object sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]: its cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and, after a finite constructible locally closed stratification, each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally a cokernel of a finite matrix over $B_Z$.

(ii) $K$ belongs to the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: it is derived $\varpi$-complete, and its derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_Z}(A/\varpi^n)_Z$ have compatible étale-origin representatives with classical constructible cohomology, all in a single cohomological interval independent of $n$.

(iii) $K$ is bounded and its cohomology sheaves, after finite stratification, are pro-étale locally $B_V\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; here $A$ and $P$ in this tensor denote constant sheaves. The stratifications in (i) and (iii) may differ. Torsion cohomology is allowed, and no completeness hypothesis is imposed in (i).

source.place: Definition 6.5.1, Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); general ring-object model comparison from the existing DAG

proof.text: Use the coefficient-limit isomorphism to identify $B_T$ with $\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ for $T=Z$ and for every stratum used below. The Cartesian coefficient isomorphisms identify restriction of $B_Z$ with $B_T$, and give exact restriction on modules. The continuous integral coefficient object in the resolution theorem is this same $p_T^*\underline A$: the norm on $E$ and $A=\{x:|x|_E\le1\}$ are those fixed in the coefficient convention. Thus all the following applications concern the original coefficient ring and ordinary derived category.

source.place: §6.5 coefficient convention; Definition 6.8.10; coefficient identification supplied by the cited DAG statements

proof.text: Every locally closed scheme stratum $S\hookrightarrow Z$ is again Noetherian, finite-dimensional, and has $\ell$ invertible. Indeed the minimal-closed-subset property for $Z$ makes its space Noetherian, so every subset is quasi-compact. Factor $S$ as closed in an open $O$; $O$ is Noetherian by the open-subscheme lemma. Intersections with an affine cover of $O$ present $S$ as spectra of quotients of Noetherian rings. Such quotients are Noetherian since ascending chains of their ideals lift to ascending chains of ideals upstairs; quasi-compactness selects finitely many of these affine charts. A strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $S$ remains strict after closure in $Z$, since intersection back with $S$ recovers it, so the dimension bound persists. Units map to units in every stratum local ring. Also $Z$ is quasi-separated: every intersection of two affine opens is quasi-compact by the same subset property.

source.place: Hypothesis checks for Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); elementary scheme-stratum reductions

proof.text: Assume (i). Fix a degree $q$ with $H^q(K)≠0$ and a stratum $S$ on which $P=H^q(K)|_S$ is locally finitely presented. Apply the integral locally-free-resolution theorem to $P$ on $S$. It supplies a short exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F_0\to P\to0$, where each $F_i$ is pro-étale locally finite free over $B_S$. This theorem allows torsion in $P$ and assumes no completeness of $P$. Its topologically Noetherian hypothesis follows from step 2. The two covers for $F_1,F_0$ need not coincide.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), finite DVR resolution argument; existing general-ring-object resolution interface

proof.text: For each $i$, $F_i[0]$ satisfies condition (ii) of the stratified-perfect characterization on $S$: use the single stratum $S$ and, on a trivializing cover, the perfect scalar complex $A^{r_i}[0]$. Hence $F_i[0]$ belongs to the completed integral category. The short exact sequence in step 3 gives the distinguished triangle $F_1[0]\to F_0[0]\to P[0]\to F_1[1]$. Closure under cones in that same characterization puts $P[0]$ in the completed category. Its condition (iii) now supplies a finite stratification of $S$ on which $P$ has finite constant scalar local models. This argument uses the theorem on the Noetherian finite-dimensional base $S$, never on the possibly non-Noetherian members of its pro-étale covers.

There are only finitely many relevant $q$ and finitely many original strata in (i). Compose each finite refinement from step 4 with its original immersion into $Z$. These give finite locally closed constructible scheme partitions of $Z$, one for each $q$. Apply the open-closed refinement theorem to these finitely many partitions: each resulting leaf has actual morphisms to the input scheme strata. Pull back the local scalar-matrix presentations along those morphisms. Exact coefficient pullback preserves their cokernels and finite free terms; their scalar entries remain the same elements of $A$. The finite-constant-model equivalence therefore gives the required models on every leaf. The bound on the cohomology of $K$ is unchanged. This proves (iii), including a common finite stratification if one is required.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), finite cohomology and stratification refinement; scalar presentations as in Definition 6.8.10

proof.text: Conversely assume (iii). The finite-constant-model lemma expresses each $B_V\otimes_A P$ as the cokernel of a finite matrix with entries in $A$, hence also of a finite matrix over $B_V$. Thus every cohomology sheaf has a locally finite presentation on its given strata. Together with boundedness this is precisely (i). This direction uses no completeness assumption and no assertion that arbitrary coefficient sections are constant.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10; the scalar-presentation implication is the cited finite-constant-model lemma

proof.text: Finally apply the stratified-perfect characterization directly on $Z$. Its condition (iii) is exactly the cohomological scalar-model condition (iii) here; its condition (i) is explicitly also the category of the detailed integral definition used in (ii). The theorem retains compatible étale-origin witnesses and a single bound for all derived reductions. Therefore it proves both (ii) implies (iii) and (iii) implies (ii), with precisely these extra clauses, not merely constructibility of each reduction separately. Steps 3–6 identify (i) with (iii), completing all three equivalences.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q64-3096e87b9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item with every cited statement open. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from the landed base. There are 0 new nodes, and the split is an assembly of existing nodes. I found no cycle (the closure of the cited nodes does not contain the item) and no re-split note. (ii)<=>(iii) is lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization applied on Z (step 7). Its detailed-category clause supplies completeness, compatible étale witnesses and the uniform [r,s], which matches Bhatt-Scholze Prop. 6.8.11(3) with Def. 6.5.1 and 6.8.10. (i)=>(iii) works as follows. Step 2 shows the strata are Noetherian, finite-dimensional and qcqs with ℓ invertible; these facts are elementary from the three Noetherian leaves. On each stratum, lem-weil-pbc-integral-lfp-locally-free-resolution gives 0->F1->F0->P->0 with F_i locally finite free. F_i[0] is a perfect constant model, the SES triangle and cone closure put P[0] in the category, and the characterization's (iii) gives scalar models. lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement gives actual morphisms to the strata, and constant models pull back. (iii)=>(i) uses det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model (finite constant model => lfp). The coefficients B_Z = lim (A/ϖ^n)_Z are the same ring in all three cited frameworks via sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x and the Cartesian clause. Edge cases checked: Z empty and K=0 are trivial; over Spec of a separably closed field an lfp module is constant; B[1/ϖ] is excluded from (ii); (A/ϖ^r)_Z has uniform reduction amplitude [-1,0]. I accept the declared tool_uses because the unit route via sk-lem-integral-models needs finite type over a field. No duplicate exists in the DAG and the item cites no SGA. Advisory only: step 5 could say in one clause that locally closed strata of the Noetherian Z are constructible.
